checks.title: Unnecessary HTTP methods enabled
checks.description: The server may accept HTTP methods that the API does not need. Assess against the API's documented method allowlist.

checks.title: HTTP OPTIONS reveals excessive methods
checks.description: The API may advertise methods that are not required for the endpoint.

checks.title: HTTP method override is enabled
checks.description: A proxy or application may honor method-override headers, which can bypass controls that only inspect the original method.

checks.title: Unsupported request content type is accepted
checks.description: The API may process a body using an unexpected media type rather than rejecting it.

checks.title: Unsupported response media type is returned
checks.description: The API may ignore the client's Accept header and return a response format that clients or security controls do not expect.

checks.title: Response Content-Type header missing
checks.description: A response with a body may not declare its media type, increasing ambiguity for clients and intermediaries.

checks.title: MIME sniffing protection missing
checks.description: Browser-facing responses may omit X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, allowing browsers to infer content types.

checks.title: HSTS header missing
checks.description: HTTPS responses may omit Strict-Transport-Security, so browsers may not be instructed to use HTTPS on future visits.

checks.title: HSTS max-age is too short or zero
checks.description: The HSTS policy may have a zero or very short max-age, reducing its protection.

checks.title: HSTS subdomain policy absent
checks.description: The HSTS header may omit includeSubDomains even when all relevant subdomains are HTTPS-only.

checks.title: Content Security Policy missing on HTML response
checks.description: An API response that serves HTML may lack a Content-Security-Policy, reducing browser-side content restrictions.

checks.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
checks.description: Browser-facing responses may omit a Referrer-Policy that limits referrer information sent to other sites.

checks.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
checks.description: Browser-facing responses may not restrict browser features through a Permissions-Policy header.

checks.title: Clickjacking protection missing on HTML response
checks.description: HTML responses may lack frame restrictions through CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options.

checks.title: Server identity header exposed
checks.description: The Server response header may disclose server software or version information.

checks.title: Technology disclosure header exposed
checks.description: Framework-specific response headers may disclose implementation details.

checks.title: Internal proxy headers exposed in response
checks.description: Response headers may reveal internal proxy, routing, or infrastructure details.

checks.title: Cross-origin resource policy is permissive
checks.description: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy may allow resources to be embedded across sites when a stricter policy is intended.

checks.title: Cross-origin opener policy is permissive
checks.description: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy may be absent or permissive on browser-facing pages that need browsing-context isolation.

checks.title: CORS allows all methods
checks.description: The CORS policy may permit every HTTP method, including methods the browser client does not need.

checks.title: CORS allows sensitive methods to untrusted origins
checks.description: The CORS policy may allow state-changing methods to a caller-supplied origin.

checks.title: CORS allows all request headers
checks.description: The CORS policy may allow arbitrary request headers from browser clients.

checks.title: CORS exposes sensitive response headers
checks.description: The API may expose internal or security-sensitive response headers to browser JavaScript.

checks.title: CORS preflight cache duration is excessive
checks.description: A long Access-Control-Max-Age may keep a permissive preflight policy cached in browsers after configuration changes.

checks.title: Cookie missing Secure attribute
checks.description: A cookie may be sent over cleartext HTTP if its Secure attribute is absent.

checks.title: Cookie missing HttpOnly attribute
checks.description: A session or authentication cookie may be accessible to client-side scripts if HttpOnly is absent.

checks.title: Cookie SameSite attribute missing or unrestricted
checks.description: A session cookie may lack a SameSite restriction or use SameSite=None, increasing cross-site request exposure.

checks.title: Cookie has an overly broad Domain attribute
checks.description: A cookie may be shared with sibling subdomains through a broad Domain attribute.

checks.title: Cookie has an overly broad Path attribute
checks.description: A cookie may be available to more application paths than required.

checks.title: Cross-origin resource sharing origin varies without Vary header
checks.description: A server that returns different CORS headers per origin may omit Vary: Origin, risking incorrect shared-cache behavior.

checks.title: Proxy trust configuration may accept spoofed client IP
checks.description: The service may trust forwarded client-IP headers from untrusted callers, affecting IP-based controls or logging.

checks.title: Host header may influence generated response URLs
checks.description: The application may use an untrusted Host header when generating redirects, links, or password-reset URLs.

checks.title: Forwarded host header may influence generated URLs
checks.description: The application may trust an untrusted X-Forwarded-Host value when constructing absolute URLs.

checks.title: Proxy protocol mismatch may expose backend behavior
checks.description: The API may respond differently to forwarded protocol headers, indicating inconsistent proxy trust or HTTPS enforcement.

checks.title: HTTP TRACE method may be enabled
checks.description: TRACE can reflect request headers and is generally unnecessary for an API.

checks.title: HTTP TRACK method may be enabled
checks.description: TRACK is an unnecessary legacy method and should generally be rejected.

checks.title: HTTP CONNECT method may be enabled
checks.description: CONNECT should not normally be accepted by an API origin server.

checks.title: WebDAV methods may be enabled
checks.description: WebDAV methods such as PROPFIND or MKCOL may expose unnecessary file-management functionality.

checks.title: HTTP method response differs across gateway and backend
checks.description: A method accepted by one layer and rejected by another can indicate inconsistent request filtering.

checks.title: Content negotiation may permit unsafe XML parsing
checks.description: An endpoint may accept XML despite only requiring JSON, potentially enabling XML parser risks if parser features are unsafe.

checks.title: XML external entity feature may be enabled
checks.description: The service may use an XML parser configured to resolve external entities. Confirm through configuration review or a controlled test environment.
checks.curl: curl -i --max-time 10 -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/xml' --data '<!DOCTYPE probe [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/hostname">]><probe>&x;</probe>' '{{baseUrl}}/__replace_with_staging_xml_endpoint__'

checks.title: GraphQL introspection may be enabled
checks.description: GraphQL schema introspection may expose types and operations. Whether this is a fault depends on exposure and access policy.

checks.title: GraphQL query depth or complexity controls may be absent
checks.description: The GraphQL service may accept deeply nested queries without suitable depth or cost limits.

checks.title: GraphQL batching may be enabled without limits
checks.description: The service may accept batched GraphQL operations without a suitable batch-size limit.

checks.title: GraphQL playground may be exposed
checks.description: An interactive GraphQL console may be accessible in production and reveal schema or enable operations.

checks.title: gRPC reflection may be exposed
checks.description: The gRPC reflection service may reveal service and method definitions to clients.

checks.title: WebSocket origin checks may be missing
checks.description: The WebSocket service may accept browser connections from an untrusted Origin. Confirm through a valid handshake in an authorized test.

checks.title: WebSocket endpoint may permit unauthenticated connection
checks.description: A WebSocket handshake may succeed without credentials where the endpoint is expected to be private.

checks.title: Webhook endpoint may not require signatures
checks.description: A webhook receiver may accept requests without a verified signature, allowing forged event submissions.

checks.title: Webhook replay protection may be absent
checks.description: The receiver may not enforce event timestamps or replay identifiers. Confirm using an approved staging event and signature.

checks.title: Webhook signature header is not enforced
checks.description: A webhook may accept requests without a signature header or equivalent authenticated delivery proof.

checks.title: Unrestricted redirect target may be configured
checks.description: A redirect parameter may allow arbitrary external destinations when only trusted destinations should be permitted.

checks.title: Health endpoint returns detailed dependency status
checks.description: A health check may expose database, queue, or downstream service names and status to unauthenticated callers.

checks.title: API version or build metadata exposed
checks.description: Version endpoints may expose build identifiers, commit hashes, or deployment details useful for reconnaissance.

checks.title: Source map or source bundle may be exposed
checks.description: A publicly accessible source map can reveal original source paths or embedded source content.

checks.title: Directory listing may be enabled
checks.description: A web server may list files in an exposed directory, potentially revealing configuration or backup artifacts.

checks.title: Backup or configuration artifact may be exposed
checks.description: A known, in-scope backup or configuration path may be publicly downloadable. Avoid broad path guessing.

checks.title: API gateway may expose a backend bypass route
checks.description: A backend service may be directly reachable outside the gateway's authentication or filtering controls. Requires infrastructure inventory to identify the backend.

checks.title: Cross-origin policy permits null origin
checks.description: The API may allow the special null Origin used by sandboxed documents and some local contexts.

checks.title: CORS allows an unencrypted origin
checks.description: The CORS policy may trust an HTTP origin, allowing browser requests from an unencrypted site.

checks.title: Sensitive response lacks no-store cache directive
checks.description: A sensitive response may omit Cache-Control: no-store and remain in browser or intermediary caches.

checks.title: Pragma no-cache directive missing on sensitive response
checks.description: A sensitive response may omit the legacy Pragma: no-cache directive for compatibility with older intermediaries.

checks.title: Cache response varies by authorization without Vary
checks.description: A response that changes based on Authorization may lack Vary: Authorization, which can cause shared-cache mix-ups.

checks.title: TLS certificate validation failure
checks.description: The endpoint may present an expired, mismatched, or untrusted certificate. curl normally fails certificate validation; do not disable verification.
checks.regex: (?i)(certificate has expired|certificate subject name .* does not match|unable to get local issuer certificate|SSL certificate problem)

checks.title: TLS certificate nearing expiration
checks.description: The endpoint certificate may be close to expiry. Use a TLS-aware scanner or certificate inspection for accurate dates.

checks.title: TLS renegotiation or legacy protocol support
checks.description: The TLS endpoint may support legacy protocol behavior. Validate with a dedicated TLS scanner and current policy.

checks.title: API accepts plain HTTP on an alternate listener
checks.description: An alternate port or hostname may serve the API over HTTP even if the primary endpoint uses HTTPS.

checks.title: Cache-control header is duplicated or contradictory
checks.description: Multiple conflicting Cache-Control headers may be interpreted differently by proxies and clients.

checks.title: Content-Security-Policy permits unsafe script execution
checks.description: HTML responses may use CSP directives such as unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, weakening script restrictions.

checks.title: Content-Security-Policy permits all sources
checks.description: A CSP policy may contain wildcard sources for scripts or default content, weakening its restrictions.

checks.title: Reflected request header appears in response
checks.description: The API may reflect caller-controlled headers, which can indicate unsafe proxy or response construction behavior.

checks.title: Error response reveals database or query details
checks.description: An error may disclose database product names, query fragments, table names, or connection details.

checks.title: Error response reveals filesystem paths
checks.description: Errors may expose absolute paths or application directory structure.

checks.title: Error response reveals internal hostnames or addresses
checks.description: Errors may disclose private hostnames, internal IP addresses, or service topology.

checks.title: API response includes diagnostic correlation details
checks.description: Responses may reveal trace identifiers or diagnostic internals beyond a safe opaque request ID.

checks.title: Potential response splitting through header reflection
checks.description: A service or intermediary may improperly reflect newline-containing input into response headers. Test only in a controlled environment.

checks.title: Content type does not match returned body
checks.description: The response Content-Type may not match its actual content, potentially triggering unsafe client parsing.

checks.title: JSONP callback support may be enabled
checks.description: A legacy callback parameter may wrap JSON in executable JavaScript rather than returning JSON only.

checks.title: Cross-origin policy permits broad subdomain patterns
checks.description: The CORS policy may trust a broad or attacker-controllable subdomain pattern.

checks.title: Untrusted origin accepted by CORS suffix matching
checks.description: Origin matching may use unsafe suffix logic that accepts domains controlled by unrelated parties.

checks.title: Authentication challenge configuration is inconsistent
checks.description: A protected route may return an error without an expected authentication challenge, suggesting inconsistent edge and application policy.

checks.title: Cross-origin policy allows credentials with wildcard-like reflection
checks.description: The service may reflect arbitrary origins while also enabling credentials, a high-risk combination for browser clients.

checks.title: TLS-only service redirects to a noncanonical or untrusted host
checks.description: The HTTPS endpoint may use caller-controlled host information to construct redirects.

checks.title: Response includes internal environment name
checks.description: Responses may disclose environment labels such as staging, development, or internal production identifiers.

checks.title: Public endpoint exposes framework actuator configuration
checks.description: Framework management endpoints may expose environment, configuration, or process information.

checks.title: Public endpoint exposes application environment variables
checks.description: A management endpoint may expose environment variables that include secrets or infrastructure details.

checks.title: Public endpoint exposes heap dump or process data
checks.description: A publicly reachable diagnostic endpoint may expose memory or process data containing sensitive values.

checks.title: Public endpoint exposes application mappings
checks.description: A management endpoint may reveal internal route mappings and service structure.

checks.title: Public endpoint exposes runtime metrics
checks.description: Metrics may disclose process, infrastructure, or workload information useful for reconnaissance.

checks.title: Default framework landing page exposed
checks.description: A default server or framework welcome page may reveal deployment details or indicate incomplete hardening.
checks.regex: (?i)(welcome to nginx|apache2 default page|it works!|spring boot|tomcat default)

checks.title: Unprotected API schema endpoint
checks.description: A schema endpoint may be accessible without credentials, revealing routes and data models.

checks.title: Unprotected API documentation UI
checks.description: An interactive documentation UI may be available without authentication.

checks.title: Debug endpoint reveals configuration values
checks.description: A debug or configuration route may return active settings, feature flags, or environment data.

checks.title: HTTP response allows caching of authorization errors
checks.description: Authentication or authorization error responses may be cached and affect later clients if cache directives are unsafe.

checks.title: API response sets a cookie without an explicit expiration policy
checks.description: A session cookie may persist longer than intended if no Max-Age or Expires attribute is set.

checks.title: Cookie uses insecure SameSite=None configuration
checks.description: A cookie marked SameSite=None must also be Secure; otherwise browser behavior may be inconsistent and cross-site exposure may increase.

checks.title: Security header is duplicated with conflicting values
checks.description: Duplicate security headers may be interpreted inconsistently by clients and intermediaries.

checks.title: Response includes permissive cross-origin embedder policy
checks.description: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy may be absent or permissive on browser applications that require cross-origin isolation.

checks.title: Untrusted request headers appear in redirect response
checks.description: The API may use caller-supplied forwarding headers when generating redirects.

checks.title: HTTP response exposes server timing details
checks.description: Server-Timing may disclose internal component names or precise processing details.

checks.title: HTTP response exposes detailed cache diagnostics
checks.description: Cache diagnostic headers may disclose internal cache topology or backend identifiers.

checks.title: API accepts unexpected query parameter for format override
checks.description: A format override parameter may switch response handling or content type unexpectedly.

checks.title: API accepts unexpected callback parameter
checks.description: A legacy callback parameter may change JSON responses into executable JavaScript.

checks.title: Production response includes test or sample data
checks.description: Responses may contain sample records, demo markers, or test identifiers indicating test data is deployed.

checks.title: Configuration backup suffix may be publicly served
checks.description: A known configuration file may have a publicly accessible editor or backup suffix. Check only paths confirmed to be in scope.

checks.title: Log endpoint or log artifact may be publicly served
checks.description: A known log route or artifact may disclose operational details, tokens, or personal information.

checks.title: Open redirect may be configured on logout or login route
checks.description: A return or redirect parameter may allow navigation to an arbitrary external site.

checks.title: HTTP compression is enabled on sensitive authenticated responses
checks.description: Compression on responses that mix secrets and attacker-controlled content may create side-channel risk in some contexts.

checks.title: HTTP request body accepted without declared content length or framing policy
checks.description: Inconsistent request framing across proxies and backends may indicate request smuggling risk. Requires specialized testing and configuration review.

checks.title: HTTP response includes permissive cross-origin policy for HTML
checks.description: Browser-rendered HTML may be accessible to unrelated origins due to permissive CORS configuration.

checks.title: Insecure redirect from API root
checks.description: The API root may redirect users or clients to an unencrypted HTTP URL.

checks.title: Production API serves an unexpected plaintext response
checks.description: A response may contain credentials or sensitive data over HTTP instead of redirecting or refusing the connection.

checks.title: Certificate hostname does not match API host
checks.description: The TLS certificate may not cover the requested API hostname.
checks.regex: (?i)(no alternative certificate subject name matches|subject name .* does not match|certificate subject name .* does not match)

checks.title: Certificate chain is incomplete or untrusted
checks.description: The server may not provide a complete trusted certificate chain.
checks.regex: (?i)(unable to get local issuer certificate|unable to verify the first certificate|self-signed certificate)

checks.title: API response leaks cloud metadata or instance identity
checks.description: A response may expose cloud instance identifiers, role names, or metadata-derived values.

checks.title: API response exposes internal service URLs
checks.description: Responses may reveal internal HTTP service URLs or private hostnames.

checks.title: API response exposes filesystem or source repository metadata
checks.description: Responses may disclose source paths, repository locations, or build workspace details.

checks.title: Production debug mode or verbose error leakage
checks.description: The API may expose stack traces, internal paths, environment details, or interactive debug tools.
checks.regex: (?i)(traceback|stack trace|exception at|debug toolbar|werkzeug debugger|development mode|\.java:\d+| at [\w.$]+\([^)]*:\d+\))

checks.title: CORS allows any origin
checks.description: The API may allow browser-based requests from any origin. Risk increases when credentials or sensitive data are involved.

checks.title: CORS reflects an arbitrary origin
checks.description: The API may copy a caller-supplied Origin into its CORS response, potentially allowing untrusted websites to read responses in a browser.

checks.title: Credentialed CORS enabled
checks.description: The API may allow browsers to include credentials in cross-origin requests. Combined with an overly broad origin policy, this can expose authenticated data.

checks.title: HTTP endpoint does not redirect to HTTPS
checks.description: The API may accept cleartext HTTP connections, which can expose requests or credentials in transit.

checks.title: Security headers missing or weakened
checks.description: Browser-facing API responses may lack transport or content-type protections. Applicability depends on whether browsers consume the API.

checks.title: API documentation route publicly reachable
checks.description: OpenAPI/Swagger documentation or an interactive API console may reveal routes or enable calls. Exposure is not automatically a vulnerability if access controls are sound.

checks.title: Metrics endpoint reveals operational details
checks.description: Health, metrics, or status endpoints may expose internal service names, versions, hostnames, or environment information.

checks.title: Server or framework version disclosed
checks.description: Response headers may disclose server or framework versions that help identify outdated components.

checks.title: Authentication may be missing on a protected route
checks.description: A route expected to require authentication may return a successful response without credentials. Route intent must be established from an API specification or policy.

checks.title: Rate limiting may be absent
checks.description: Repeated requests may not receive throttling or quota signals. This is most concerning on login, recovery, OTP, payment, or expensive operations.
checks.curl: for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null --max-time 10 '{{baseUrl}}/__replace_with_authorized_low_impact_route__'; done

checks.title: Oversized request limits may be missing
checks.description: Request bodies may be accepted without suitable size limits, creating denial-of-service or storage risks. Use a staging environment for size-limit testing.
checks.regex: (?i)(413\s+Payload Too Large|request entity too large|content too large)

checks.title: Default or test credentials may be enabled
checks.description: Approved sample credentials or test accounts may remain active in production and provide unauthorized access.

checks.title: Debug or test routes may be exposed
checks.description: Development, test, or administrative routes may be deployed publicly and disclose state or provide privileged operations.

checks.title: Cache policy may allow sensitive responses to be stored
checks.description: Responses containing account or personal data may be cacheable by shared intermediaries if cache directives are missing or permissive.

checks.title: TLS protocol configuration may be weak
checks.description: The service may support obsolete TLS protocol versions or weak ciphers. HTTP response checks alone cannot reliably establish TLS configuration.
checks.regex: (?i)(SSL connection using TLSv1(?:\.0|\.1)?|SSL connection using TLSv1\.0|SSL connection using TLSv1\.1)

checks.title: Production secrets may be exposed in API responses
checks.description: Responses may contain credentials, tokens, private keys, or cloud secrets due to configuration or data-handling mistakes.
